title: Use the discovery chain
objective: Reorder: connectors, outcome, metrics, agent idea and workflow.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: Discovery runs in one direction: from what the business needs to how you would measure it. Starting from a solution, such as "let's build an agent," skips the facts that decide whether it will work.

items: **Business outcome:** what changes for the business, and who owns that result.
**Use case:** the actor and the job they need to do.
**Workflow:** how the job is done today, with its steps, handoffs, and systems.
**Data:** the information the job needs, where it lives, and who can access it.
**Success metrics:** the evidence that the outcome improved.

blocks.caption: Discovery chain for faster case resolution
head: Link
Example
rows: Higher support throughput without lower quality
A support agent finds the approved answer for a case
Review case → search sources → check with a peer → draft → respond
Case context, knowledge base articles, past resolutions
Handle time, paired with resolution quality checks

blocks.x: If you start with a complex agent design, you lock in assumptions before you know the data or the workflow. Following the chain exposes missing facts and dependencies, such as an unowned knowledge base or a permission model nobody has checked, while the design can still change. An agent idea is one possible implementation. It is never the starting requirement.
Work the chain from the top. Starting at connectors or agent ideas produces technology in search of a problem.

blocks.title: The discovery chain
blocks.alt: A five-link chain worked from top to bottom: business outcome, use case, workflow, data, and success metrics. Each link is discovered in that order.
